**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white paper plate is about 18 cm in diameter, a typical small paper plate. Area = 3.14 × (9)² ≈ 254 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** About 25 whole almonds. No oil, sauce, or dressing is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The almonds cover roughly 30% of the plate (about 75 cm²), which fits a single loose layer of about 25 pieces at roughly 3 cm² each.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Almonds pile about 1 cm high, so gross volume ≈ 75 cm² × 1 cm ≈ 75 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole nuts pack loosely, with a bulk density of about 0.5 g/ml. That gives about 38 g. Counting pieces directly, 25 almonds × ~1.2 g each ≈ 30 g. I'll take about 30 g as the best estimate.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Almonds are about 600 kcal per 100 g (roasted). 30 g × 6 ≈ 180 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 25 almonds is a modest handful, so 30 g and about 180 kcal is plausible. It is far below a full-plate meal, as expected from the small visible amount.
